page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m1.3xlarge is a compute-oriented virtual server within the ecs.u0 family, provisioned on a KVM hypervisor utilizing the x86_64 CPU architecture. The instance features 12 dedicated vCPUs accompanied by 12.0 GB of system memory, yielding a strict 1:1 ratio of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs provisioned on the host.

Local storage is not bundled with this configuration, necessitating the deployment of external network-attached volumes for operating system disks and persistent file storage. Network capability includes a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses by default, requiring secondary assignment for external routing.

The low memory-to-vCPU allocation delivers high compute thread concurrency at the expense of memory density. This resource profile optimizes cost efficiency for workloads that demand substantial parallel processing power without heavy per-thread RAM overhead. Primary workload fits include CPU-bound batch tasks, compilation pipelines, continuous integration testing agents, and lightweight distributed microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m1.3xlarge is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual server operating on a KVM hypervisor. The instance features 12 dedicated vCPUs and 12.0 GB of system memory, establishing a focused 1:1 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 1.0 GB per core. The hardware configuration provides a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. There are zero GPUs, and no local disk storage is bundled, requiring complete reliance on remote network-attached block storage for all operational and operating system data needs. With its dedicated core allocation and low per-core RAM density, the instance trades overall memory capacity for concurrent execution threads. This makes the configuration an efficient hardware fit for CPU-bound distributed processing, lightweight batch computational pipelines, continuous integration runners, and microservices that require multi-core concurrency without demanding large in-memory data structures.
